challenge_1_is_the_sweep_a_re_reading_or.alpha_star_is_a_correct_inverse: CONFIRMED, algebraically and empirically. max_acceptance_within(a) = max{coverage[i] : risk[i] <= a} (coverage is strictly increasing, so taking within[-1] is the max, not merely the last). Therefore max_acceptance_within(a) >= c iff (exists i)(risk[i] <= a and coverage[i] >= c) iff a >= min{risk[i] : coverage[i] >= c}. alpha_star computes exactly that minimum and it is attained, so it is the least such alpha. It uses np.min over ALL reachable indices rather than a first crossing, which is what keeps it correct where the running risk is non-monotone. 20,000 randomised trials found no violation of reachability, minimality or the None case.
challenge_1_is_the_sweep_a_re_reading_or.the_upper_bound_argument_holds: CONFIRMED and I checked the step the ADR leaves implicit. A threshold rule accepts exactly the eligible groups whose score clears the threshold, which is a prefix of the score-sorted order; so its empirical accepted set IS a point on this curve, and a certificate additionally requires a risk UPPER bound <= alpha, which implies empirical risk <= alpha. Hence oracle max acceptance at alpha upper-bounds any certificate's acceptance at that alpha, on this split. The 'rules alpha out, never in' direction is therefore structurally sound.

challenge_4_is_the_grounding_oracle_soun.verdict: CONFIRMED as a finding — the conclusion is arithmetically forced and is NOT an aggregation artefact. But the JUSTIFICATION given for it ('the reading most generous to each system') is REFUTED as stated.
challenge_4_is_the_grounding_oracle_soun.attack_1_does_the_restriction_ever_raise: It does, and the ADR does not say so. Dropping a member with loss 0 (a valid-empty prediction against empty gold scores F1 = 1.0) RAISES that group's mean loss. Measured on the certification split: ZS 0 groups rise / 16 fall; FS 24 rise / 64 fall; QA 21 rise / 132 fall. The restriction is net-generous in aggregate (group mean loss falls: ZS 0.992332 -> 0.984332, FS 0.957993 -> 0.951267, QA 0.607090 -> 0.581738) but it is NOT uniformly generous, so 'the reading most generous to the system' is false at the unit level.
challenge_4_is_the_grounding_oracle_soun.attack_2_is_there_a_strictly_more_genero: Yes, and it moves the baselines off 0.0000. I ran a variant that keeps the FULL population of 1,396 groups, marks every group eligible, and sets every non-content-bearing document's loss to 0 (i.e. a fix that also makes the repaired documents correct). Certification split, max acceptance at alpha = 0.20: FS 0.0000 -> 0.021490, ZS 0.0000 -> 0.007163, QA unchanged at 0.020057. So the bolded '+0.0000 exactly' is specific to the drop-the-documents construction, not a property of every defensible grounding counterfactual. In fairness that variant is a CORRECTNESS oracle, strictly stronger than a grounding oracle, and even it leaves both baselines an order of magnitude below the 0.20 floor.
challenge_4_is_the_grounding_oracle_soun.attack_3_is_the_zero_an_aggregation_arte: REFUTED — the zero is arithmetically forced and survives every reading I could construct. On the restricted population the group mean loss is 0.984 (ZS) and 0.951 (FS). To reach 20% acceptance at alpha = 0.20, the best-scoring 20% prefix must have mean loss <= 0.20, which caps the OVERALL mean at (0.2*0.2 + 0.8*1.0) = 0.839 no matter how the scores sort. 0.984 and 0.951 both exceed 0.839, so no threshold rule, no score, and no re-aggregation can put those systems at the floor. I also ran the restriction with the ORIGINAL 1,396-group denominator (generous on loss, conservative on coverage): still 0.0000 for both baselines, 0.0358 for QA. The finding is robust; only the exact QA movement figure is construction-dependent.
challenge_4_is_the_grounding_oracle_soun.attack_4_do_vanishing_groups_flatter_the: No, they work against the baselines' apparent benefit in one direction and for it in another, and both were checked. The restriction removes 580 (ZS) and 649 (FS) groups entirely, shrinking the coverage denominator by 42-46% — a large generosity on the coverage axis. It also removes every ineligible group (all retained documents are 'valid' by construction), so the ADR 0009 all-members-valid acceptance ceiling is lifted: ZS's eligible set goes 376/1396 -> 816/816 and FS's 712/1396 -> 747/747. Both baselines are handed more than double the eligible population AND a denominator roughly half the size, and still return exactly 0.0000. That is the strongest single piece of evidence that this is a real finding.
challenge_4_is_the_grounding_oracle_soun.what_must_change: The conclusion may stand; the justification must be replaced. 'The reading most generous to each system' should become the arithmetic bound, which is stronger, checkable and construction-independent: the restricted-population mean loss (0.984 ZS, 0.951 FS) exceeds the 0.839 ceiling compatible with 20% acceptance at alpha = 0.20, so no grounding counterfactual that leaves those systems wrong when they ground can reach the floor. See correction R5.
challenge_4_is_the_grounding_oracle_soun.on_the_within_system_caveat: The restricted-population caveat ('not a deployable acceptance rate, not comparable across systems') is present in the ADR, in the artifact interpretation string, in the module docstring, in the write-up and in the claim ledger's limitations. That is adequate and consistently repeated.

The accurate statement is that the figures are not comparable, and that ours is far above the only extraction datapoint they report. Had it returned an empty set, verifying a ledger outside a checkout would have reported every claim's evidence as untracked — noise that would train a future agent to pass require_tracked=False habitually, which is how fail-closed gates become fail-open in practice. Getting that distinction right unprompted is the mark of the change being understood rather than applied.
item_1a_tracked_evidence_gate.one_precision: git ls-files reports the INDEX, so a file that has been git-added but never committed counts as tracked. The function name untracked_evidence is exactly right; the docstring and the commit message say 'committed', which overstates by one step. A staged-only artifact would pass this gate and still not reach a reader. Trivial to fix in wording; worth fixing because this gate's whole purpose is that its guarantee is precise.
item_1a_tracked_evidence_gate.windows: The POSIX-separator normalisation is present and correct; I confirmed the gate works on this Windows checkout.

item_1b_pending_verification_tripwire.verdict: FAILS the attack — but the failure is not the one you expected, and the answer is to NARROW it, not to revert
item_1b_pending_verification_tripwire.you_asked_whether_the_regex_buys_too_lit: I measured it rather than argued about it. Of 18 verified_by strings that genuinely describe pending verification, 14 PASS: 'under review', 'in progress', 'review scheduled for Plan 4 close', 'reviewer assigned, report to follow', 'unreviewed', 'no reviewer yet', 'self-assessed by the implementer', "author's own check", 'draft review only', 'provisional', 'will be verified at Plan 4', 'verification outstanding', 'review in flight', 'n/a'. Four are caught. So as a detector of unverified claims it has roughly a 22% hit rate on natural phrasing.
item_1b_pending_verification_tripwire.the_finding_that_decides_it: Of 8 strings describing COMPLETED verification, 3 are BLOCKED — including the entirely natural 'independent review complete; no items pending' and 'reviewed 2026-07-22; P6 fix still pending'. Meanwhile 'self-assessed by the implementer' and 'trust me' both pass. The discrimination is close to INVERTED on natural phrasing.
item_1b_pending_verification_tripwire.the_harm_neither_of_us_named: That inversion is not merely useless, it is actively harmful in a way I did not anticipate and you did not raise. The rule applies pressure toward VAGUENESS in exactly the field the honesty doctrine depends on. An author who writes a detailed, honest verified_by that mentions an outstanding item is blocked; an author who writes 'reviewed' passes. A rule that penalises specificity in a provenance field is worse than no rule, because the field's entire job is to record what verification actually happened. That, not the low hit rate, is why it cannot stay as written.
item_1b_pending_verification_tripwire.ruling_narrow_do_not_revert: Anchor the match to the LEADING token. The regression that actually occurred was a verified_by BEGINNING 'pending independent review of ADR 0011'. A leading anchor — roughly ^\s*(pending|awaiting|unreviewed|provisional|tbd|tbc|not yet)\b — catches that exact regression and produces ZERO false positives across all eight completed-verification strings I tested, including both that currently break. It will still miss 'self-assessed by the implementer', and that is fine: a tripwire that catches its own regression cleanly is honest, whereas one that inverts on natural phrasing is not.
item_1b_pending_verification_tripwire.and_name_it_for_what_it_is: Rename or re-document so it cannot be read as a verification gate. PENDING_VERIFICATION and the error message both currently read semantic. It is a REGRESSION TRIPWIRE for one phrasing family and cannot detect an unverified claim in general. Put the false-negative examples above into ADR section 6 so the next agent knows the shape of the hole rather than inferring from the constant's name that the hole is closed.
item_1b_pending_verification_tripwire.why_not_revert_to_recording_only: Because the tracked-evidence half must stay regardless — it is a genuine gate and reverting the commit would lose it — and because a correctly-anchored tripwire is free, fails safe, and prevents a recurrence that actually happened once. Your instinct to split the defect into two changes of different kinds was right; my P5 bundled two unlike things and your split was better. Keep splitting them: describe the two halves with DIFFERENT strength claims rather than under one commit message, because one is a gate and one is a tripwire and conflating them is how the tripwire acquires the gate's authority.
item_1b_pending_verification_tripwire.structural_fix_stays_deferred: Correct. verified_by as a typed reviewer-record path plus verdict, existence-checked and tracked-checked like evidence, is the real answer, it does re-classify, and it belongs to its own review. ADR section 6 records it. Leave it there.

item_2a_what_6_3_actually_says_and_what_.verdict: The finding is real. The FRAMING of it is wrong in one direction and too modest in another.
item_2a_what_6_3_actually_says_and_what_.wrong_direction_the_gloss_was_not_strict: This is the correction that matters most and it must not be written up the other way. The repo's gloss — 'the headline target must not be relaxed after seeing this' — does NOT come from 6.3 and is not an over-strict reading of it. It is a faithful rendering of 6.2's fourth bullet, which I read in the primary text: 'all systems far above `alpha`: expect heavy abstention or infeasibility; do not relax `alpha` after seeing certification.' That is the branch this project is in, unambiguously — base risks 0.9923 / 0.9580 / 0.6071 against alpha = 0.20. So the binding constraint is exactly as strict as the repo assumed, ADR 0011's central safety argument was aimed at the right rule, and only the section number was wrong. Do not let 'section 6.3 permits a sweep' become 'the constraint was weaker than we thought'. It was not. If anything, finding 6.2's bullet shows the caution was required rather than excessive.
item_2a_what_6_3_actually_says_and_what_.too_modest_you_do_not_need_6_3: Section 9.1 licenses the object by name: 'An infeasible system remains infeasible; its descriptive risk-coverage curve may be plotted but no test threshold is selected.' All three systems are infeasible. Both artifacts select no threshold and carry certifies_nothing: true. That is the alpha-frontier, permitted explicitly, on exactly the condition it satisfies — and it is far stronger cover than the descriptive branch of a sentence about target sweeps.
item_2a_what_6_3_actually_says_and_what_.the_qualification_i_must_state: 9.1 sits under section 9, Final in-domain evaluation — the stage ADR 0010 descoped. So this is a READ-ACROSS, not a literal hit, and it must be presented as one. It is a strong read-across: it would be perverse to read the plan as permitting the descriptive curve on the sealed, one-shot final split while forbidding it on a certification split that is already open, and ADR 0010's descope leaves 9.1's licence with no other application. State the read-across openly. Do not present it as direct cover.

item_2b_is_the_descriptive_branch_readin.verdict: YES, as stated — you were right to suspect it. But you do not need it, so re-cite rather than stretch.
item_2b_is_the_descriptive_branch_readin.why_it_is_too_convenient: Grammatically, 'small, predeclared' modifies 'sweep', and BOTH status branches ('simultaneous correction or clearly descriptive status') attach to that sweep. The sentence licenses a small predeclared sweep under either status. It does not license a large post-hoc sweep by selecting the weaker of the two statuses and discarding the modifiers. Twenty post-hoc points against three predeclared ones is not a stretch the text supports.
item_2b_is_the_descriptive_branch_readin.the_purposive_argument_if_you_still_want: It is available and it is genuinely good, but it must be labelled purposive rather than textual. 'Small' and 'predeclared' are both SELECTION and MULTIPLICITY guards: small bounds the family of tests, predeclared prevents choosing which points to report after seeing them. The alpha-frontier discharges that hazard by a stronger route than compliance. It runs no test and computes no bound, so 'simultaneous correction' is not merely satisfied but literally inapplicable — there is nothing to correct. And it publishes the ENTIRE range, so nothing whatever is selected; a three-point predeclared sweep still involves choosing three points, and is on that dimension strictly weaker. Line 483 supports the labelling branch: 'Secondary target sweeps ... are simultaneous-corrected where a formal claim is made or explicitly labelled exploratory' — and diagnostic_only / certifies_nothing is that labelling.
item_2b_is_the_descriptive_branch_readin.the_residual_exposure_state_it_plainly: One hazard that 'small' guards against is NOT discharged by publishing everything: the rhetorical one. Twenty points give a reader twenty places to land, and the curve shown to alpha = 1.00 has QA reaching 0.907 acceptance at alpha = 0.60 — a visible 'if only the target were higher' story that three points bracketing 0.20 would not create. That is precisely 6.2's hazard. It is currently defended by the wording discipline — the necessary-not-sufficient paragraph, the forbidden-wordings table, the ruling-out-only boundary — and NOT by the plan text. Say so. A defence that is known to be doing work is maintained; one that is assumed to be structural is not.

item_2c_the_section_neither_of_us_cited.verdict: 8.5 No post-hoc rescue is where an adversarial reader starts, its escape clause is STRICTER than 6.3's, and ADR 0011 does not engage it. This is the single most important addition.
item_2c_the_section_neither_of_us_cited.the_text: Section 8.5 forbids rescuing a failed hypothesis by, among other moves, 'changing `alpha`, `delta`, acceptance floor or loss' and 'reporting only empirical rather than certified acceptance'. Its escape clause: 'Such analyses may appear as labelled exploratory work if predeclared AND multiplicity-aware, but they cannot change the primary conclusion.' Note that conjunction. 6.3 offers correction OR descriptive status; 8.5 requires predeclared AND multiplicity-aware. If the alpha-frontier fell under 8.5, the descriptive label would not be enough and predeclaration is absent.
item_2c_the_section_neither_of_us_cited.my_ruling_it_does_not_bind: 8.5 governs analyses that RESCUE a failed hypothesis. The alpha-frontier rescues nothing: it makes the null broader, not narrower — the failure now holds across the entire range below 0.406 rather than at one point — and the documents forbid using it to indicate a workable target. An analysis that generalises a null is the opposite of a rescue. And 8.5's own operative condition, 'they cannot change the primary conclusion', is satisfied exactly: all three systems remain infeasible at the frozen target, H1 and H2 remain both_infeasible, and no certificate exists anywhere.
item_2c_the_section_neither_of_us_cited.but_silence_is_not_available: The nearest bullet — 'reporting only empirical rather than certified acceptance' — is close enough to the alpha-frontier's surface form that a hostile reader will reach for it, and the frontier does report only empirical/oracle acceptance because there is no certified acceptance to report. ADR 0011 section 1 must engage 8.5 explicitly and give the argument above. Leaving the strictest applicable-looking section uncited, in an ADR whose entire purpose is to establish that a sweep was safe, reads as avoidance whether or not it is.

item_3_the_doc_reference_exclusion.verdict: Reasoning SOUND, implementation appropriately narrow, but the safety rests on an assumption nothing enforces
item_3_the_doc_reference_exclusion.what_is_right: The distinction is correct and worth keeping: a result document naming a test asserts that a guarantee currently holds and is checkable; an accepted plan naming a test issues an instruction about work not yet done. And an accepted plan is a historical record — amended by appended note, never rewritten to match what happened — so forcing its references to resolve would corrupt the record or create dead files. The implementation is scoped to the FILENAME (endswith on 'accepted-plan.md'), not to the directory, so real result documents sitting beside the plans are still checked. That is the narrow version, correctly done.
item_3_the_doc_reference_exclusion.the_gap: You named the risk yourself — 'the exclusion becomes a place for real dangling references to hide' — and it is real, because the exclusion's safety rests entirely on accepted plans never being edited, and NOTHING ENFORCES THAT. There is no test pinning the four copies to their hashes. I verified all four against _pmo by hand today; that guarantee expired the moment I finished.
item_3_the_doc_reference_exclusion.required_fix_and_it_is_cheap: Pin all four accepted-plan.md files to their sha256 in a test. The hashes are recorded in external_signal_fourth_pass above. Then the exemption is safe BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by trust: an edit to an accepted plan fails loudly instead of silently widening a hole in the doc-reference check, and the 'historical record, never rewritten' rule stops being a convention and becomes an enforced property. This converts your stated risk from something to remember into something that cannot happen.
